_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: AuthHeader() trims the configured token and sends it as `Authorization: ApiToken <token>` with no double prefix
handfixes.why: SentinelOne rejects a bare token: every management API call must carry `Authorization: ApiToken <token>`. The spec declares this (`x-auth-value-prefix: 'ApiToken '` on the APIToken securityScheme) but cli-printing-press does not consume that extension - still true at 4.32.5, which emits `return token` - so every reprint regenerates config.go with broken live auth while go build, go test, shipcheck and dogfood all stay green (the 2026-06-05 4.22 reprint and the 4.24 reprint both re-hit it; only a reviewer reading client.go caught it). The guard also tolerates an operator who pasted the prefix themselves (no double prefix). authheader_test.go pins both directions. This was a silent hand-fix from the first print onward; recorded on the 4.32.5 reprint (2026-09-28). REPRINT 4.34.0 (2026-10-24): the press now honours x-auth-value-prefix and emits ensureAuthScheme("ApiToken", token) (case-insensitive, no double prefix); the hand part left is the TrimSpace of the configured token. The ensureAuthScheme assert stays so a press that stops honouring the prefix fails this ledger.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Upstreamed for the prefix at 4.34.0 (x-auth-value-prefix). The token trim is still hand-applied.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282. UPDATE 2026-09-28 (reprint to cli-printing-press 4.32.5): the press now emits doctorInfoKeys/doctorIsInfoKey and the --fail-on info-key skip natively, and no longer emits the "but auth was accepted" line; doctor_verdict.go therefore drops its own copy of the info-key map (it merges the three connector keys the native map lacks in an init()), while the placeholder refusal, the no-credential ERROR row and doctorUnexpectedStatus remain hand-wired into doctor.go. REPRINT 4.34.0 (2026-10-24): the press generates doctorBaseURLIsPlaceholder in doctor.go (RFC 2606 hosts only, so it misses the shipped your-console.sentinelone.net default); the connector's check is kept as doctorBaseURLIsShippedPlaceholder in doctor_verdict.go and doctor.go calls both.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For sentinelone the manifest gained: SENTINELONE_BASE_URL. server.json gained: SENTINELONE_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: SENTINELONE_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out. UPDATE 2026-09-28 (reprint to cli-printing-press 4.32.5): the 4.32 binary also reads SENTINELONE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN (cmd/sentinelone-mcp/main.go, bearer for --transport http) and PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE (internal/platform/profile.go, tenant-gated client profile); both are declared optional on all three channels, following the datagate/threatlocker shape, because check_env_schema.py (hard-fail in the CI guards job) treats an undeclared read as a credential nobody is prompted for. The 4.32 binary also reads SENTINELONE_USER_AGENT (cliutil.EnvOverride in internal/client/client.go and internal/cli/deliver.go, an optional User-Agent override); it is declared optional on all three channels following the huntress 4.32.5 shape. check_env_schema.py only sees this read once it resolves package-qualified helpers (cliutil.EnvOverride) - the same resolution that turns SENTINELONE_BASE_URL from a false 'declared but never read' into a read. REPRINT 4.34.0 (2026-10-24): the press manifest declares only SENTINELONE_API_TOKEN; the onboard union restores the other four, and the 4.34.0 runtime switches SENTINELONE_MCP_READ_ONLY (preset 1) and SENTINELONE_NO_LOCAL_DATA are declared on all three channels.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP server's --transport http listener sets ReadHeaderTimeout so one client cannot hold it open by dribbling request headers
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press 4.32.5 gives every MCP server a --transport http mode (streamable HTTP behind bearer auth) and the generated cmd/sentinelone-mcp/main.go http.Server literal sets no header-read deadline, so a single client could hold the listener open indefinitely by sending request headers one byte at a time (Slowloris). gosec G112 flags exactly this shape and the security gate raised it as P1 on the 4.32.5 reprint (2026-09-28; same finding and fix as the huntress 4.32.5 pilot and datagate since PR #317). The fix adds ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second to the http.Server literal. A reprint regenerates main.go without the field and go build stays green, so this marker is the only thing that notices. code_only because the explanatory comment above the field also names G112 - the assert must be satisfied by the field itself. DURABLE FIX belongs in the press's mcp main.go template; file via printing-press-retro.

handfixes.summary: firewall-control copy-rules / move-rules / set-location refuse stray positionals, and name the new `item-<name> by-category` path when the pre-reprint spelling `<name> by-category` is used
handfixes.why: On cli-printing-press 4.24 the generator registered two constructors under the same name in firewall-control, so `copy-rules`, `move-rules` and `set-location` were groups whose only child was `by-category` and the leaf endpoints were unreachable. The 4.32.5 reprint (2026-09-28) disambiguated them: the three names are now the leaf POST endpoints and the by-category operations moved to `firewall-control item-<name> by-category`. The generated leaf commands accept and ignore positionals, so a script still typing `firewall-control move-rules by-category --stdin` silently POSTed its body to a different mutation (/firewall-control/move-rules) - found by the Codex review of the reprint (P1). firewallControlLeafArgs rejects any positional before a request is built. A reprint regenerates the three leaf files without the Args line and go build stays green; these asserts notice. TestFirewallControlOldSpellingSendsNothing proves the old spelling sends zero requests (it fails, with one request sent, when the Args line is removed) and TestFirewallControlOldBySpellingIsRefused proves the bare leaf and the new item-* path still resolve. REPRINT 4.34.0 (2026-10-24): the press now generates the three leaves with cobra.NoArgs and a hidden by-category child that refuses with the rename message, so firewall_control_compat.go is gone; the hand-written behaviour test stays and covers all three names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit Args: cobra.NoArgs on endpoint commands that declare no positionals, which would make a mistyped subcommand an error fleet-wide; this entry then reduces to the migration message.

handfixes.summary: `users login-by-token --token` help text shows `<your-user-token>` instead of the 80-hex-character sample token the vendor spec carries
handfixes.why: The SentinelOne spec's example for the login-by-token `token` parameter is a real-looking 80-character hex user token, and cli-printing-press copies spec examples verbatim into flag usage text. gitleaks (generic-api-key, the CI guards job) fails the build on it, and it teaches operators and agents to paste a token-shaped literal. The 0.1.x tree carried this as an unrecorded hand-edit; the 4.32.5 reprint (2026-09-28) regenerated the file and silently restored the sample, which only the guards job's gitleaks step caught. code_only so the assert is satisfied by the usage string itself.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Replace the example in the vendored spec (or have the press redact token-shaped examples on credential parameters); then this entry flips to upstreamed.

handfixes.summary: cmd/sentinelone-mcp/main.go declares `var version = "0.0.0-dev"` and passes it to server.NewMCPServer, so release.yml's `-X main.version=<tag>` stamps the real release into serverInfo.version (issue #322, PR #323)
handfixes.why: The 4.32.5 reprint graft (PR #343) dropped the `var version` declaration and hardcoded "0.0.0-dev" in the NewMCPServer call, although the press template main_mcp.go.tmpl at v4.32.5 emits the var. The Go linker silently ignores -X for a symbol that does not exist (build exit 0, no warning), so release.yml's stamp could never land; the Release run for sentinelone-v0.2.0 (https://github.com/Servosity/msp-skills/actions/runs/36472932792) refused the build when the initialize probe answered serverInfo.version='0.0.0-dev', and 0.2.0 was burned. Proven locally with a real initialize JSON-RPC over stdio: after the fix `go build -ldflags '-X main.version=9.9.9'` answers 9.9.9. code_only because the explanatory comment above the var names the ldflags mechanism; the assert must be satisfied by the declaration itself.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: None needed at the press: main_mcp.go.tmpl already emits the var and passes it. The loss was in the reprint graft, so this entry guards the next graft; retire it after a reprint confirms the var survives natively.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 10 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: accounts expire-now expire-an-account (POST /accounts/{account_id}/expire-now); agents abort-scan (POST /agents/actions/abort-scan); dv cancel-running-query (POST /dv/cancel-query); firewall-control item-move-rules by-category (POST /firewall-control/{firewall_rule_category}/move-rules); firewall-control remove-tags remove-rule-tags-by-category (POST /firewall-control/{firewall_rule_category}/remove-tags); remote-scripts run (POST /remote-scripts/execute); reports delete (POST /reports/delete-reports); settings clear-pending-emails (POST /settings/notifications/cancel-pending-emails); singularity-marketplace enable-or-disable-application (POST /singularity-marketplace/applications/{mode}); sites expire-now expire-site (POST /sites/{site_id}/expire-now). REPRINT 4.34.0 (2026-10-24): the press still aliased agents_abort-scan.go and settings_clear-pending-emails.go; removed by hand again. The other eight carry no alias natively. 4.34.0 also aliased singularity-marketplace install-applications (POST /singularity-marketplace/applications installs an application) as create; removed by hand and added to the test.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown); the title of an HTML page returned where JSON was expected. Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

handfixes.summary: `ranger exposure` reads the Ranger device inventory (resource ranger-table-view, /ranger/table-view), not the credential-group records
handfixes.why: The novel read the resource named `ranger`, which syncs /ranger/cred-groups/details (credential records), as the device inventory, so every Ranger-discovered unmanaged device was invisible and credential records with an ip field were counted. Found on the 4.34.0 reprint; the test was seen failing on the 4.32.5 shipped code. A replay that restores the shipped ranger_exposure.go brings the bug back.

handfixes.summary: root.go registers fleet-health with a literal rootCmd.AddCommand so press dogfood sees `fleet-health stale`
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 dogfood's command walker sees only literal AddCommand calls, so with the generated addNovelCommandIfAbsent(rootCmd, newNovelFleetHealthCmd(flags)) the `fleet-health stale` leaf was invisible and the root framework `stale` false-matched it (dogfood FAIL command-depth mismatch). A reprint restores the generated line and dogfood fails again: visible, not silent.

handfixes.summary: Novel site groupings key on siteId (two accounts' same-named sites stay apart); dossier, recurrence and blast-radius join endpoints by agent id, not hostname
handfixes.why: Codex round 1 on the 4.34.0 reprint: grouping by site name merged two accounts' Default sites, hostname joins merged distinct machines, recurrence-after-mitigation did not require a later detection on the same endpoint, and blast-radius counted detections instead of agents. Every grouping now emits site_id. Hand-written novel files; a replay of the 4.32.5 copies brings the merges back.

handfixes.summary: versions, versions rollout and fleet-health judge each OS against its own current agent version (current_by_os, rollout target_by_os); decommissioned agents never pick the target
handfixes.why: Codex round 1 on the 4.34.0 reprint: SentinelOne ships agent packages per OS, so one fleet-wide modal version marked every macOS or Linux agent outdated against the Windows build. JSON change: current_version/modal_version became current_by_os.

handfixes.summary: `versions plan` (upgrade worklist per site and OS, reachable vs offline) is registered by the hand parent versions.go
handfixes.why: New novel on the 4.34.0 reprint. The 4.32.5 versions.go does not register it, so a replay of the shipped copy drops the command silently (only the scaffold help test notices). --target requires --os and a dotted numeric version; an --os with no agents is refused.

handfixes.summary: Agent liveness is isActive, read by one tri-state helper (agentLiveness: online only when isActive is the JSON boolean true, offline only when it is false, anything else unknown), never networkStatus, which is the network-isolation state. `agents reclaim` lists only an explicitly inactive agent with a known last check-in at least --days ago; unknown status is counted (unknown_status), never listed; hostname twins and decommissioned agents are never listed. fleet-health, fleet-health summary, posture and versions plan never count unknown as online; whatchanged reports went-offline as active -> inactive and isolation (network connected -> disconnected) separately.
handfixes.why: An MSP decommissions what reclaim prints and schedules upgrades from versions plan. networkStatus is the state of the 'Disconnect from network' action (spec.yaml POST /agents/actions/disconnect isolates an endpoint and the agent keeps talking to the console; POST /agents/actions/connect reverses it); whether an agent checks in is isActive (GET /agents 'Include only active Agents'; threats agentIsActive 'Agents currently connected to the Management Console'), with lastActiveDate the last check-in. Reading networkStatus as liveness meant reclaim never listed a powered-off seat that was never isolated (LAPTOP-OFF-90D: networkStatus connected, isActive false, silent 90 days), fleet-health counted it online and an isolated live server offline, versions plan listed the dark laptop as reachable, and whatchanged reported an isolation as 'went offline' (adversarial review 2026-10-26, .review/helpers/online/findings.json). Earlier (Codex round 2 on the 4.34.0 reprint) a 'connecting' status was listed; the tri-state keeps that fail-closed: only an explicit boolean is read.

handfixes.summary: A 2xx or cached answer that repeats a held credential in any encoding is withheld and the call fails; three marked lines in the generated client.go route every success return through s1_success_funnel.go
handfixes.why: The canonical funnel covers error text only; a successful answer reaches stdout, MCP tool results and the store. Codex rounds 1 and 2 on the 4.34.0 reprint: a token echoed raw, Base32-encoded, behind a duplicate JSON key, or split by CR/LF in a binary body passed. Every value is checked as received and with whitespace, control and format characters dropped; JSON is walked token by token; values within the canonical 1 MiB cap get full recursive decoding (canonical funnel plus Base32, base64, hex, escapes, ROT13, UTF-16) and a match against every encoded form of each credential; a value over the cap withholds the whole answer (no windowed fallback). apply_secret_funnel.py does not know these three client.go sites: a funnel re-apply must keep them. The canonical funnel files stay byte-identical.

handfixes.summary: sync records a fleet history capture holding exactly the rows its own walk wrote, so whatchanged, versions rollout, threats verdicts and threats mttr history have two captures to diff
handfixes.why: store.CaptureFleetSnapshot existed since the first print and nothing called it, so every history command said 'needs at least 2 syncs' forever (zero call sites on the 4.32.5 shipped tree). s1_snapshot_hook.go wraps the generated sync through registerNovelCommand (no generated file edited). An ordinary sync re-reads all agents and threats (beginFleetWalk resets each watermark); --since, --param/--resource-param, --max-pages, --latest-only and --dry-run record no capture. Codex round 2 on the 4.34.0 reprint: membership compared second-resolution synced_at, so a row removed between two walks in the same second stayed in the later capture. Membership is now per walk (fleet_walks + per-connection triggers recording the walk's own row and sync_state writes); a capture fails closed with a warning when membership cannot be proven; capture stamps are unique and ordered. The timestamp-based CaptureFleetSnapshotSince is removed.

handfixes.summary: threats mttr and threats recurrence take the earliest end of an allowlisted, explicitly successful mitigating action as the mitigation time; never updatedAt, an undo action or an unknown action
handfixes.why: Codex round 1 on the 4.34.0 reprint: MTTR used updatedAt. Round 2: a later successful un-quarantine (documented inverse action in spec.yaml /threats/mitigate/{action}) was taken as completion, so a threat contained in 1h read as a 48h SLA breach. Only quarantine, remediate and rollback-remediation with status success and no failure signal count; a threat with action records but none qualifying is mitigated_unmeasured.

handfixes.summary: Every CLI command that changes the SentinelOne tenant (endpoint commands whose pp:method is not GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, plus import) refuses before any client exists unless --yes or --dry-run is given; four read-only POSTs are the allowlisted pp:path values.
handfixes.why: P1: with SENTINELONE_BASE_URL at a loopback stub and a fake token, `sentinelone-cli agents abort-scan --json` sent POST /agents/actions/abort-scan and exited 0 with no confirmation; the same held for all 209 endpoint write commands (network isolation, uninstall, decommission, remote-scripts run, deletes), while the MCP twin sentinelone_execute already required confirm=true. The gate is one call in the root PersistentPreRunE (write_confirm_gate.go), fail-closed on the method annotation so a future generated write command is covered without an edit; the refusal is a usage error (exit 2) with a JSON envelope carrying confirmation_required under --json/--agent. A --yes saved in a run profile does not count. Help examples of gated commands are rewritten at tree build so none shows a refused invocation. A reprint that drops the root.go call leaves the gate file dead; write_confirm_gate_test.go drives every write command against a fake API and fails if any sends without --yes.

handfixes.why: On press 4.34.0, agents.fetch-firewall-logs, agents.fetch-firewall-rules, agents.fetch-logs, agents.get-installed-apps-for, agents.actions.fetch-files and threats.fetch-file carry NeedsConfirm: false, so sentinelone_read sent them without confirm and SENTINELONE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 did not refuse them. handfixes.summary: The generated recipe-intents test binds the recipe's public example SHA1 to a variable named staticArg, not token, so gitleaks' generic-api-key keyword rule does not fire on it
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 emits one `if token := "<static arg>"` block per recipe argument in internal/mcp/recipe_intents_test.go; the sentinelone recipe's example hash 3f5a9c2e... (a public example from the research brief, also shown in README and page.json) then reads as a key assignment and fails the repo's gitleaks gate. Spec-encode follow-up: use a low-entropy example hash in the research recipe.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Use a low-entropy example hash (e.g. 0000...0001) in the sentinelone research recipe so the generated test needs no edit.

handfixes.summary: No credential an API read returns is kept on disk or handed to an MCP agent without confirm: sync never pulls agent passphrases or Ranger credential details, every store and cache write drops secret-named fields, old stores are scrubbed, MCP results withhold secret fields unless confirmed, and secret reads need confirm
handfixes.why: Publish-step adversarial review (2026-10-24), P1 with the real binaries: a default `sync` stored every agent passphrase (GET /agents/passphrases, the SentinelCtl unlock secret) and site/group registration tokens in the local SQLite store, and the MCP sql and search tools, available under SENTINELONE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1, returned them. Fixed as a class with fleet precedent (threatdown, watchguard, servosity, connectsecure): one shared rule (internal/cliutil/s1_secret_fields.go: secret resources by spec path, secret field names by normalized substring) used at every choke point. Generated-file edits are marked lines: sync.go (refusal in RunE and syncResource; agents-passphrases and ranger out of defaultSyncResources), channel_workflow.go (archive list), data_source.go (write-through), client.go (response cache), store.go (mergeIncomingResourceData renamed ...Unscrubbed so a reprint that restores the name fails go build instead of dropping the scrub), cmd/sentinelone-mcp/main.go (result middleware). The MCP NeedsConfirm for secret reads is set at package init from the shared rule (internal/mcp/s1_secret_reads.go), so code_orch.go is not edited.

handfixes.summary: A store written by an older build is scrubbed once, at its first read-write open, over every table: never-stored credential partitions deleted, secret-named columns cleared, secret-named JSON fields removed at any depth, the search index rebuilt; gated by StoreSchemaVersion 14, so an older binary refuses the store afterwards
handfixes.why: Codex review round 2 (2026-10-26), P1: the old-store scrub walked seven hand-picked tables, so an older store's typed table (actions with a passphrase in data) kept the value and MCP sql with a column alias returned it. The scrub now discovers every ordinary table from sqlite_master (identifiers validated and quoted through one helper), runs in the same transaction as the v14 stamp (a failure leaves the store below 14, so the next open scrubs again), and rebuilds resources_fts from the scrubbed rows. The generated store.go carries the version bump as a marked line; a compile guard (const _ = uint(StoreSchemaVersion - secretScrubSchemaVersion)) breaks go build if a reprint resets it to 13. The generated schema_version_test.go asserts the one-time FTS rebuild the scrub causes. A future change to the field rule must bump both versions together.

handfixes.summary: Every MCP tool but sentinelone_execute with confirm: true refuses a call whose arguments name a credential-tier resource, path or table in any spelling (agents passphrases, Ranger credential details and groups, uninstall password, login by token, regenerate-key tables); a CLI child the MCP server spawned refuses the same at the resource resolver
handfixes.why: Adversarial review round 2 (2026-10-26), P1: MCP tail and export on the resource "ranger" fetched GET /ranger/cred-groups/details with no confirm and returned the Ranger credentials verbatim (their key names miss the field rule), while sentinelone_read refused the same endpoint. Fixed at one choke point: a tool-handler middleware registered in the generated cmd/sentinelone-mcp/main.go checks every argument string at any depth (decoded and raw, SQL text normalized) against the one credential-tier list in internal/cliutil/s1_secret_fields.go; the generated internal/cli/resource_paths.go returns through mcpCredentialTierPath so a spawned CLI child (SENTINELONE_MCP_CHILD=1) refuses too. The store holds no credential-tier rows by construction (secret-never-persisted, secret-store-scrub-every-table), which covers SQL the text check cannot read. A test walks every registered tool so a future reader is covered.
